system.name: MoniTor
system.one_liner: Training-free online video anomaly detection: a VLM captions streaming frames and an LLM scores anomalies using memory, a scoring queue and behaviour prediction.

content.variant_note: four columns, each following one real CCTV clip from its frame to a plain caption, then a scored caption with prediction, then a class chip
content.argues: MoniTor turns streaming surveillance clips into captions, predicted next behaviour and anomaly scores, and names the incident across different cameras: Abuse, Robbery, Explosion, Fighting.
content.subject: Four real CCTV clips followed from frame to caption to scored caption plus prediction, each ending in a class chip.

lessons.what_to_learn: Repeat one identical stack (input still, intermediate text, final text with score, class chip) across several columns, one per incident type; the repetition shows breadth and real text with a few coloured key words shows what the system actually writes.
lessons.suits: Teaser figures for perception or monitoring systems where a few real inputs, generated text outputs and a category label show the capability without a method diagram.

evidence: Illustration of MoniTor which detects abnormal events across multiple surveillance perspectives.
MoniTor identifies critical security incidents: Abuse, Robbery, Explosion, Fighting and so on.
As shown in Fig. 1, our MoniTor can precisely and efficiently identify various abnormal events.

summary: MoniTor is a training-free approach to online video anomaly detection: streaming frames go to a vision-language model, and a dual memory, a scoring queue with an anomaly prior and behaviour prediction guide an LLM in scoring anomalies over time. Figure 1 is a teaser built from four real CCTV clips, one per column. Each column stacks the clip frame, a plain caption, a longer 'Caption with score' that also holds a predicted next behaviour and an anomaly score, and a coloured chip naming the incident (Abuse, Robbery, Explosion, Fighting). Blue line-art person and camera icons sit beside the boxes, red and yellow words highlight anomalous actions and places, and a glossy camera logo with the Monitor wordmark heads the figure. No arrows are drawn.
